purpose: Common-name aliases from the S&P 500 constituents' 'Security' column for names the SEC titles miss (receipts/store.py SECURITY_ALIASES: ordinary aliases; SHORT_NAMES: lookup-only names, which a claim's company or an Ask lookup resolves by but running text never counts). Each entry is a Security name, or its short name, that is not already one of its company's keys, with the decision and its reason, and the common names the S&P 500 QA of 2026-10-31 found missing (source 'common name'). Fourth round (sources 'common name (...)'): the names people use for every one of the 499 companies, derived the same way for all (COMMON_NAMES: ordinary aliases, never display names; SHORT_NAMES: lookup-only).
rule: An alias is normalize_entity(Security). It has at least two words, or is one distinctive word that is not an English word (/usr/share/dict/words, plural and possessive forms included), a common first name (/usr/share/dict/propernames) or surname, a US place name or a market index; when unsure it is blocked. A short name is the Security name without generic trailing words (Laboratories, Scientific, Motor, Motors, Company, Companies, Corporation, Corp, Incorporated, Inc, Co, Group, Holdings, Holding, plc, Ltd, US), never leaving a generic head such as International or General or ending on a small word; two words or more make an ordinary alias, one word a lookup-only name. Places, indexes and ordinary phrases are lookup-only or blocked, and every key must name exactly one company across all lookup keys of the 499 companies (tests/test_entity_scale.py). Decisions of 2026-10-31: Cigna, IQVIA, Emcor and L3Harris allowed; Moody's, Lowe's and DuPont lookup keys in WORD_NAMES; Hartford, Old Dominion and Dow blocked; Ball, Casey's, Cognizant, Domino's and Flex (blocked at first) lookup-only. From the S&P 500 QA (2026-10-31, G4): the common names Truist and Lockheed lookup-only (one word), Martin Marietta an ordinary alias (two words). Fourth round (QA round 2, G4): for each company, the Security and SEC names without The, Inc./Incorporated, Corp./Corporation, Co./Company/Companies, Holdings, Group, Ltd., plc, '& Co.' and N.V./S.A., and their first one or two words, apostrophes dropped and hyphens read as spaces; plus nine names people use that are not first words (Gallagher, Con Edison, ConEd, Con Ed, P&G, Amex, Sands, Pure Storage, Citi). A candidate that doesn't resolve is an ordinary alias when it is distinctive and how the company is known (one word: not an English word, first name or surname, and six letters or more); lookup-only when it is how the company is known but an English word, surname, first name, place, phrase or shorter; blocked when it starts another company's name (a tie: Huntington for HBAN and HII, American, General, United), names another company, is generic, or is not how the company is known.
normalization: normalize_entity folds accents (NFKD, combining marks dropped) after NFKC, so 'Estée Lauder' is 'estee lauder' rather than 'est e lauder'. No stored key changes (checked on all SEC titles, Security names, ALIASES and the 62 stored companies; the only changed normalization is the Security name 'Estée Lauder Companies (The)').
